output_text: description: This guide defines definitive best practices for writing maintainable, performant, and robust Ansible code. Always structure your Ansible content into roles and collections. Roles encapsulate specific functionalities, while collections group related roles, modules, and plugins. Role Scoping: Each role or module must focus on a single, well-defined task. Avoid monolithic roles. Fact Modules: Create dedicated `_info` or `_facts` modules/tasks for gathering information, rather than overloading existing ones. Enforce strict YAML formatting. File Start: All YAML files must begin with `---`. Indentation: Use two spaces for indentation, never tabs. Quotes: Quote strings only when necessary. Prefer single quotes. Use double quotes for escaping characters or multi-line strings. Colon Spacing: Use exactly one space after a colon in key-value pairs. Structured Map Style: Always use the structured map style for module parameters, not the legacy `key=value` style. Booleans: Standardize on `true`/`false`. Adopt consistent `snake_case` naming. This applies to variables, tasks, files, and role names. Prefix role names with the collection namespace. Variables, Tasks, Files: My_Task_Name: "Install Software" my_variable: "value" name: Install software. Write idempotent tasks. Favor declarative modules over imperative `command` or `shell`. Atomic File Operations: Always use `atomic_move` (implicitly via `copy`, `template` modules) for file modifications. Manage configurations with templates and structured variables.
